headline: On November 13, 1995: Mozambique joins the Commonwealth without British ties
captionCards: First nation to join the Commonwealth without British colonial history
Reinvented global diplomacy by proving shared values can unite nations beyond empire
instagramCaption:
Mozambique became the first nation to join the Commonwealth of Nations without ever being part of the British Empire.

This historic move marked a shift in global diplomacy, as the country from Southeast Africa entered a new international alliance.

Maputo, the capital and largest city, hosted key diplomatic events during the transition.

A surprising detail: Mozambique is bordered by the Indian Ocean to the east and separated from Madagascar by the Mozambique Channel.

Its membership redefined what it meant to be part of the Commonwealth, showing that shared values could transcend colonial history.
